artifacts.synopsis: After Metro Atlanta Presbytery dissolved Grace North Atlanta, a complaint challenging that action was declared administratively out of order for lacking a signature. Wills then complained to the SJC. The SJC held the SJC complaint was not properly before it and was administratively out of order: under BCO 43-2, a complaint must first go to the court whose act is challenged, and Presbytery had not yet addressed that ruling. Wills could file with Presbytery within 30 days. No merits ruling on the dissolution.

artifacts.title: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church
artifacts.synopsis: An individual appealed directly to the SJC, alleging her church effectively excommunicated her without process, failed the Matthew 18 process, and spiritually abused her by social isolation. The SJC dismissed as premature, without reaching the merits, because there was no record of a judicial decision by the church or of an appeal to Evangel Presbytery, the next higher court; it stated she could proceed only by providing such evidence. The severity of excommunication did not excuse that prerequisite. The SJC asked Presbytery to obtain the session's written response to her letter.

artifacts.synopsis: An appeal challenged a presbytery's conviction of a minister for divisive behavior and its indefinite suspension from office and the sacraments. The SJC affirmed: the charge was lawful because publicly publishing disagreement with the session after it acted violated his ordination vows to subjection and peace/unity, even though “divisive” is not a constitutional term; the censure was not unjust absent repentance; procedural errors did not require reversal or remand. A dissent argued the charge failed BCO 29-1’s Scripture-proof requirement.

artifacts.synopsis: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority.

artifacts.synopsis: A complaint arising from Central Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to prosecute TE Stephen O. Stout and to recognize his accusers as voluntary prosecutors was denied. The SJC framed two issues and answered both yes: the Presbytery could constitutionally adopt its Investigative Committee report and decline judicial process, because the Committee found no “strong presumption of guilt” under BCO 31-2; and it could refuse voluntary-prosecutor status, because BCO 31-1/31-3 left discipline to the Presbytery and made any voluntary prosecutor subject to its approval. The complaint was denied on both issues.

artifacts.synopsis: After a congregation voted to ask that all ruling elders' official relationships be dissolved without censure, the Session concurred and requested an interim Session. The SJC denied the elders' complaint, holding that BCO 24-6b extends by good and necessary deduction from one elder to multiple identified elders. Dissolution ended their service on that Session but did not divest them of office. Because both the congregation and Session requested it, BCO 13-9 and 15-2 authorized Presbytery to appoint an interim Session. A separate constitutional inquiry was denied without explanation.
